notes: Read-only Tier-1 capture on a healthy running cable_guy. CPU/RSS via tools/sample_resource.sh (--match cable_guy/main.py, 60 samples, label running_baseline; PID 174, comm python3). SLO via tools/probe_http.sh on read-only GETs (--repeats 40). Live interfaces observed: eth0, usb0, wlan0, uap0. NO mutating routes exercised: POST/DELETE /address, POST /dynamic_ip, POST/DELETE /dhcp, POST /set_interfaces_priority, POST /host_dns can change the vehicle's IP/route/DNS and lock out the operator's own connection; those journey outcomes remain Unknown. Raw evidence: /tmp/cableguy_sample.json, /tmp/cableguy_slo.json.

route_inventory.note: Read-only GETs probed on the live Pi; mutating routes deliberately not exercised (network-lockout hazard).

running_baseline.note: GET contracts on a healthy running cable_guy (idle, no mutating actions).

GET /cable-guy/v1.0/interfaces.body_predicate: array including eth0, usb0, wlan0, uap0

slo_running_baseline.note: GET /host_dns is ~1.2 s because it shells out (cat/lsattr on /etc/resolv.conf) per request; the other reads are fast (7-26 ms).

running_baseline.method: /proc stat deltas, top-style (100 == 1 core), PID 174 python3 cable_guy/main.py
running_baseline.note: Periodic CPU spikes from the interface-manager watchdog reconciliation loop; RSS flat at ~53 MB.

navigator.notes: cable_guy manages host wired interfaces regardless of flight controller; platform-independent on this Pi4/Navigator host.

state_machine: none (service_definition states: Unknown; a manager watchdog reconciles interface state periodically, not a discrete state machine)
settings_mutations: Not exercised. Mutating routes persist to /root/.config/cable-guy/settings-2.json (SettingsV2) and to /etc/dhcpcd.conf / /etc/resolv.conf; not mutated during this read-only capture.
